Subject: Stepped delivery + safeguarded true-up proposal for Lyrical AI Dedicated

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is a proposal that aims to balance Lyrical's need for predictable committed capacity with the flexibility your product/market uncertainty requires. Key points up front:

- Term: 3-year committed Dedicated footprint with an annual prepay option (you prepay each year).
- Step schedule (GPU equivalent / TPM carve): Year 1 = 25% (8 GPU-equivalents), Year 2 = 50% (16 GPU-equivalents), Year 3 = 100% (32 GPU-equivalents).
- Discounts: Year 1 = 15% off list, Year 2 = 22% off list, Year 3 = 30% off list (applied to committed capacity).
- True-up cadence: quarterly usage true-ups. Unused prepaid capacity can be: (a) rolled forward as credit, or (b) converted to on-demand credit at 60% of equivalent list price.
- Early-exit / downscale protection: if Lyrical needs to scale down after Year 1, we propose an early-exit credit equal to 50% of remaining prepaid value (amortized) plus a 90-day winding period for capacity handover.
- Operational: Dedicated pools will be reserved in us-west; we will support canary rollouts and per-route fallbacks to lower-cost model variants during onboarding windows.

I attached an XLSX showing an illustrative cash flow + Delivery_Timeline and a CSV with the per-unit price ladder. This version intentionally keeps Year 1 slightly conservative on discount while giving meaningful upside once you hit full runway in Year 3.

Questions for you: which of the following three items are priority for Lyrical right now?
1) Maximize near-term cash savings (bigger Year 1 discount, larger up-front prepay)
2) Minimize downside risk and maintain elasticity (stronger early-exit terms / higher on-demand conversion)
3) Operational predictability for Q1/Q2 (firm delivery windows and SLAs with penalties)

If you’re open, I can loop in our finance lead (Ben) and our delivery PM (Lauren) to pick the most appropriate contract language.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: Draft_MSLA_v3.docx, Delivery_Timeline.xlsx, Pricing_Schedule.csv
From: Maya Singh <maya@lyricalai.com>

Subject: Re: Stepped delivery + safeguarded true-up proposal for Lyrical AI Dedicated

Dev —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I like the stepped approach — it aligns with our engineering roadmap. A few immediate asks from our side:

- Flexibility on Year 1: we may need to start slightly below 25% if a pilot takes longer. Can we make Year 1 20% with the ability to convert additional committed units into on-demand at a known rate within the first 90 days?
- Early-exit credit: 50% of remaining value gets us part way there but not enough given our VC covenants. Would you consider 65% for the first 18 months (then 50% thereafter)?
- True-up transparency: the quarterly true-up needs to be tied to a simple usage dashboard and a firm cap on the per-token on-demand rate we can convert to — we cannot have open-ended conversion pricing.
- Legal will want SLAs and a clear definition of "GPU-equivalent" (e.g., A100-80GB equivalent) and a delivery calendar for when dedicated racks are online.

If you can accept provisional 20% Year 1 and the 65% early-exit for 18 months, we can escalate to procurement for a quick review. Happy to do a call tomorrow 9am PT.

Thanks,
Maya
CTO, Lyrical AI

Maya —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for flagging procurement/legal items. Based on internal ops/pricing, here is a revised counterproposal:

1) Term & Step schedule: unchanged (3yr, 20% / 50% / 100% by year). We accept your ask to set Year 1 at 20% with a documented 120-day accelerator window to purchase additional committed units at the Year 1 price.

2) Discounts & list adjustment: We will accept the 65% early-exit credit for cancellations within the first 18 months but will modestly reprice the committed ladder (+8% list uplift) to offset amortization. Net effective discount to you remains ~18% Year 1, ~24% Year 2, ~29% Year 3 after uplift. (See attached Pricing_Schedule.csv for numeric line items.)

3) True-up & conversion: Quarterly true-ups remain; unused prepaid converts to on-demand credit at 60% of list price with a hard on-demand conversion cap equal to 1.4x our committed amortized unit rate. We will publish a usage dashboard (SLA: 48hr data latency) to support the true-up process.

4) SLA & definitions: We added explicit "GPU-equivalent" language (A100-80GB perf baseline), a delivery calendar with canary windows, and a remediation credit schedule in the attached MSLA draft.

If this is acceptable we can issue a draft redline-friendly DocuSign and aim for procurement review this week. Would you like Ben or Lauren on the procurement call?

Best,
Dev

Dev / Maya —

Legal here. We reviewed the MSLA and have two high-level redlines we need discussed before procurement signs off: (1) the early-exit credit needs clearer trigger language ("material product-market change" is vague) and (2) the conversion rate cap must be expressed as a dollar-per-GPU-month ceiling rather than a multiplier to avoid interpretation disputes.

We can live with the 65% for 18 months if you agree to:
- Replace the subjective trigger language with an objective set (bankruptcy, force majeure, sustained under-utilization below 40% for 4 consecutive quarters, or investor-mandated wind-down).
- Set the conversion ceiling at $X,XXX per GPU-month (we propose $12,000 as a cap) and allow quarterly re-evaluation tied to published cloud spot indices.

If you can accept those two items we will route the redline within 48 hours. Otherwise we will need to escalate internally which will delay the timeline.

Alex Romero
Head of Legal, Lyrical AI
